### Claim 5 — Cross-org isolation invariant

**Verdict:** PASS

**Evidence:**

The acceptance test exercises a stronger invariant than "Agent owning Org-A must not have synth-grant over Org-B": it tests "Agent with NO Owns edges gets denied". Specifically at `acceptance_m5_3_owner_grant.rs:184-213`:

```rust
let stranger = AgentId::new();
let stranger_owned = repo.list_agent_owned_orgs(stranger).await.unwrap();
assert!(stranger_owned.is_empty(), "an unrelated agent owns no orgs");
let stranger_ctx = CheckContext { ..., agent_owned_orgs: &stranger_owned, ... };
let denied = check_permission(&stranger_ctx, &manifest, &NoopMetrics);
let err = denied.expect_err("non-owner must NOT resolve [Allocate]");
assert_eq!(err.code, "NO_GRANTS_HELD");
assert_eq!(err.status.as_u16(), 403);
```

**Mechanical isolation analysis**: the synth-loop at `engine.rs:247-261` iterates `ctx.agent_owned_orgs` only — a per-CheckContext slice populated by the call-site from `Repository::list_agent_owned_orgs(ctx.agent)`. Each call-site builds its own slice keyed by `ctx.agent`; an Agent A owning Org-A has its slice = `[A]` only, so the synth-loop will emit a candidate URI `org:<A's-id>` only. Org-B (which A does not own) cannot surface because the slice does not contain B. The audit-prompt's narrower "Org-A owner has no synth over Org-B" invariant is mechanically guaranteed by this slice-based design.
